# FDreamUIFaceBrush

<!-- Generated by the DreamGUIReferenceDocs commandlet from reflection. Edit the header, not this page. -->

Declared in `Public/Controls/DreamControlStyles.h`.

An optional skin for a control part's procedural-rect face.

Empty means the face stays the plain rounded rect -- the built-in look. Set a texture (or an
atlas sprite) and the face draws it inside the same silhouette: corner radius, borders and the
selectable's tint all keep working, because the skin is the rect's BODY texture, not a different
visual. Deliberately not the image brush: a control face never stops being a rect.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Category | In the details panel | From Blueprint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Image` | `TObjectPtr<UObject>` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | One slot for the image, the Slate-brush shape: a plain texture or an atlas sprite, whichever is dropped in. Two typed slots with a "sprite wins" rule was a worse panel for the same data. |
| `Tint` | `FColor` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | Multiplied over the image -- Slate's tint. A separate channel from the style's state colours: those ride the visual's colour via the selectable's transition, this rides the rect's BODY colour, and the two multiply. |
| `ScaleMode` | `EDreamRectBlockTextureScaleMode` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | Stretch / FitIn / Envelop -- the rect's three, matching UMG's Stretch / ScaleToFit / ScaleToFill. |
| `DrawMode` | `EDreamRectBlockTextureDrawMode` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | Image / Box / Border -- Slate's DrawAs, and the last thing this brush could not say. |
| `Margin` | `FMargin` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | The nine-slice edges, in TEXTURE pixels -- Slate's Margin, and the number the artist has: a border eight pixels wide in the file stays eight pixels wide on screen at any rect size. Ignored unless DrawMode slices. |
| `ImageSize` | `FVector2D` | Face Brush | yes | read / write | The image's own drawn size -- Slate's ImageSize. Zero means no opinion: the part keeps the size its style gives it. Non-zero wins over the style's size field on the parts that carry one (the toggle's box and mark, the radio's box and dot, the slider's handle). |
